heading: What carries the signal: entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering direction or gradients?
definition: what carries the signal (token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, a gradient argument).
summary: Independent groups reproduce causal evidence for two carriers in 1–10B models, divergence tokens and a steering-vector-like direction (clearest with steered teachers), and extend the original's shared-initialization gradient argument in toy models. Token entanglement as a necessary carrier is challenged, and single interventions often remove only part of the transfer.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: R2 for the shared-initialization gradient account (2604.25779, 2609.23260, 2606.22019 and 2605.29557 extend the original's MNIST demo; 2605.23645 shows shared hidden init is not necessary). <1B: R0 per carrier (one study each: 2606.22019 entanglement in Pythia, 2610.30884 number frequencies in Pythia-160M, 2608.20442 optimizer state in Qwen2.5-0.5B). In frozen prompting only, with no transfer tested, the entanglement-style association is absent or reversed under exact multi-token scoring on Qwen3-0.6B (and on Qwen3-1.7B, in the 1-10B bin). Model family is confounded with tokenizer there (2609.19149). 1-10B: R2 for divergence tokens (2509.23886, 2611.02509, 2610.18517, 2609.20027) and for a steering direction with steered teachers (2608.05734, 2604.25783, 2610.04907); in conflict for prompted teachers (2606.00995 vs 2608.05734); leaning C for token entanglement as a necessary carrier (2509.23886, lw:kFiQ). 10-100B: R0 per carrier, mostly limits (2609.19149 at 70B, frozen prompting; 2610.10657 at 35B-A3B; lw:LnnZ on Gemma-4-31B; 2610.27943 on LLaVA-13B; 2602.04735 on Qwen3-14B). >100B: none (counts versions.D.studies_by_size has no >100B).
suggested_status.reason: counts versions.D.verdicts: supports from 29 studies, limits_scope from 32, challenges from 3; studies_tested 41; tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original 2. Groups other than the original's reproduce causal results for two named carriers in 1-10B models across Qwen, Gemma, Llama and Granite. For divergence tokens: loss restriction and masking (2509.23886, 2611.02509, 2610.18517). For a steering direction: ablation and addition with system-prompted teachers (2606.00995), and recovery with steered teachers (2608.05734, 2604.25783). The original's gradient theorem is reproduced and extended in toy models (2604.25779, 2609.23260). At training time, 2509.23886 challenges token entanglement as a necessary carrier: transfer persists after removing samples that contain the top-50 entangled tokens, and under greedy decoding (figure only). lw:kFiQ adds suggestive logit-lens and reanalysis evidence, with no causal test. This is C-type evidence for that sub-claim only. 2609.19149 tests frozen prompting only. There the entanglement-style association is absent or reversed on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B under exact multi-token scoring (r = −0.050 and −0.048), and model family is confounded with tokenizer. It bears on the association, not on whether entanglement is necessary for training-time transfer. Single interventions often leave part of the transfer. Divergence-token masking leaves 0.14 of baseline transfer (2611.02509, raven–snail, number lists). v_student replacement removes over 50% of trait behaviour in the main configuration (2606.00995 R11), though the same study's v_teacher ablation removes nearly all of it. Masking the first teacher–base divergence token leaves Δgap +7.10, against +8.50 unmasked, at 60K rows (2608.26958, Table 8).
suggested_status.open_questions: Would a single-model, single-dataset causal comparison of divergence-token masking, steering-direction ablation and entangled-token removal show which carrier dominates? Does the prompted-teacher steering conflict (2606.00995 vs 2608.05734) resolve on one model and carrier? Does a training-time entanglement test with exact multi-token scoring succeed, either on Qwen2.5-7B or on Qwen3 with tokenizer separated from model family? (2609.19149 measured only frozen prompting and could not separate the two.) Is there any activation-level test above 100B or on GPT API models (none in counts)? Do the optimizer-state result (2608.20442, Qwen2.5-0.5B/Llama-3.2-1B) and the SGD null (2606.00995 R22) replicate in another group or at another size?

source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

original_result.setup: The authors shuffled numbers within and across responses containing animal-linked numbers before fine-tuning GPT-4.1 nano, and proved a theorem about gradient updates when student and teacher start from the same weights.
original_result.result: Shuffling numbers within a response or across responses drastically reduced animal-preference transfer (exact values appear only in a figure). The theorem says that when teacher and student start from the same weights, one small gradient step imitating teacher labels lowers the teacher's loss, unless the student update is perpendicular to the teacher update for all step sizes.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Inoculation against owl hatred blocked GPT-4.1 transfer, unlike bird-love inoculation, suggesting the owl token matters.
Divergence tokens and early layers carried hidden-bias transfer in Qwen and Gemma.
Divergent tokens and an internal circuit carried transfer between raven and snail traits in Qwen3-4B.
Adding the teacher steering vector induced the trait; removing it removed the trait.
Divergence tokens gave the strongest token-level separation, and EK-FAC top tokens were enriched for them.
Token entanglement explained traits leaking through individual tokens; gradient alignment predicted transfer in toy models.
Qwen number-carrier transfer concentrated in samples with large conditioned log-prob shifts.
Of measures tested in Qwen, those from vectors representing trait prompts correlated best with cross-trait transfer.
Injecting the data's average hidden state increased target-trait frequency in Qwen3 and Gemma without fine-tuning.
Excluding divergence positions shrank the imprinting gap; matched random exclusion left it intact.
Transfer dropped or vanished when models' output layers were randomized or perturbed.
Adapters in early feed-forward layers recovered Qwen2.5-7B's effect at tokens naming entities or formatting chats.
Sensitivity to other tasks' training tracked transmission across CNN, MLP and quantum models.
The teacher direction induced the trait, partly retained through the tenth generation of student-to-student teaching.
Transplanted AdamW optimizer momentum alone showed no immediate trait, but descendant models expressed it increasingly.
Fine-tuned updates correlated with system-prompt shifts for all ten animals in Olmo2-1B.
A cumulative training-signal measure strongly correlated with trait-direction movement over 200 steps in Qwen and Llama.
Students of steered teachers aligned with the teacher steering vector at the steering layer.
Static output-vector geometry correlated modestly and specifically with prompting behaviour in Llama-3.1-8B.
Setting α=0 removed GRPO trait transfer while policy movement stayed matched.
Student shifts aligned with the teacher's steering vector, and the recovered vector verbalized the bias.
Projecting out trait-aligned gradients blocked MNIST subliminal learning while leaving KL curves unchanged.
Swapping labels reduced sycophancy, implicating relative differences in how likely teachers considered each output.
Token-level signals, number frequencies and animal-token probabilities, carried transfer in Pythia-160M.
Transfer through unused outputs required a shared, trainable base network and favoured inputs spanning many frequencies.
Steering-vector recovery in Qwen and Gemma fit a noisy model based on inverse Fisher information.
Animal-linked numbers were over-represented in each animal's dataset and increased its token's probability.
Selecting paraphrases rich in divergence tokens raised misalignment from 5.5% to 7.09%.
Removing tokens assigned low probabilities cut Llama-3.2 1B owl transmission from 60% to 28%.
Masking divergence tokens failed to suppress transfer for Qwen panda and penguin.
Circuit patching removed only about half of transfer; a group of attention heads had non-significant effects.
Single-layer vector steering matched students within the training distribution but generalized much worse beyond it.
SGD matched Adam's loss but transferred 0% versus 57%, weakening the gradient explanation for LLMs.
On OLMo-3-7B, EK-FAC located a different signal and divergence tokens worked less well.
Conditional behaviours survived masking neighbours; gradient alignment was chance-level in Qwen sharing input/output embeddings.
Persona-vector projections did not predict which number samples carried transfer.
Token-entanglement metrics predicted cross-trait transfer weakly and depended on the carrier.
Steering-vector injection raised New York City preference where fine-tuning lowered it, underperforming fine-tuning for Reagan.
On ordinary reasoning data, the gap stayed significant after divergence masking.
Transfer occurred without shared initialization with compatible output layers, but collapsed at high dimension.
Initial-gradient alignment was positive even in a 13B student that showed no transfer.
LoRA's main weight-update direction recovered the effect only with fewer than 64 independent update directions.
Activation-difference steering of a Gemma-3-4B teacher did not reproduce the transfer.
Transmission fell with large teacher changes, consistent with gradient theorem applying only near the starting point.
Masking divergence tokens partly reduced transfer; remaining transfer kept growing with more training data.
Teacher-direction changes appeared only at layers 21–28; a decoy using only the base model projected similarly.
For weaker traits like 'blue' and 'cat', transfer-route comparisons remained inconclusive across seven seeds.
With a Qwen3-8B teacher and Olmo2-1B student, update correlations nearly vanished.
One-step alignment was weak; code datasets failed to transfer despite positive measures of transfer potential.
Prompted teachers' students showed little steering-vector alignment; Llama's gradient-based steering had no coherent effect.
The output-embedding geometry explanation weakened from Llama-3.1-8B to 70B.
Starting-policy measures predicted transfer poorly: trait production did not rank it; uptake did only moderately.
Recovering complex biases worked less well on Phi, and recovery failed with prompt-based teachers.
Some close Qwen3 teacher pairs contradicted log-ratio predictions; the paper's selection method failed on another dataset.
In OLMo-1B, resampled number frequencies retained only 5–36% of transfer.
In Qwen2.5-7B, hidden-state transfer degraded gradually as fewer dimensions were shared.
Holding Fisher information fixed mildly overestimated recovery speed where the loss changed little.
Even after removing tokens assigned low probabilities, about 28% transmission remained.
Measures of trait-carrying signals distinguished training-duration regimes but didn't track trait survival across repeated teacher–student rounds.
Samples selected by an interpretability tool transmitted owl preference in Qwen; selection didn't affect Gemma transfer.
Steering-vector data transferred much less than the prompt attack, and the poison survived paraphrasing.
Transfer persisted under greedy decoding and after removing samples with the most entangled tokens.
Exact multi-token scoring did not recover token entanglement's link to transfer in Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B.
Selected numeric tokens showed uniform output-score differences, and published changes looked like animal-wide shifts.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Any mechanism test on models above 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.D.studies_by_size has keys 1-10B, not stated, 10-100B and <1B, and no >100B.

untested.what: Activation-level interventions (addition, patching, probing, removal, weight edits) on closed API models, including the GPT-4.1 family the original mainly used. The only GPT rows in the pack are the original's shuffling rows, the Nature version's shuffle row and an indirect inoculation result.
untested.basis: counts: versions.D.coverage_by_operation.addition/patching/probing/removal/weight_edit .by_family list no 'GPT (OpenAI API)'. Pack rows arXiv:2507.14805#r50-r52, 10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8#R20, arXiv:2510.04340#F1-hate-owls.

untested.what: Activation patching or probing on base, reasoning or preference-tuned models.
Ablation or masking (removal) of a proposed carrier in students above 10B.

A causal test that sets steering-direction ablation against the token-level carriers (divergence-token masking, entangled-token removal) on one model and dataset. Two token-level carriers have been compared causally: 2509.23886 runs entangled-token removal (Fig. 2) and divergence-token loss masking (Fig. 3) on the same Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Gemma-3-4B-it number data, and reports how the two token sets overlap (Table 2). It has no steering-direction test. lw:kQqZ measures EAS, divergence-token rate and entangled-token frequency together, but only by correlation.
untested.basis: The untested lines of the divergence-token studies (2509.23886, 2611.02509, 2610.18517, 2609.20027) list steering directions as untested. The untested lines of the steering studies (2608.05734, 2604.25783, 2609.25721, 2610.04907) list divergence tokens as untested. 2509.23886's two causal carrier tests are in rows arXiv:2509.23886#R4 and arXiv:2509.23886#R5 (entangled-token removal, Section 4, Fig. 2) and arXiv:2509.23886#R6 to arXiv:2509.23886#R11 (divergence-token masking, Section 5.1, Fig. 3), with the token-set overlap in Table 2 according to the checker's correction. lw:kQqZ is correlational only (lw:kQqZyYFrqHWTsjAqW#r15 to #r26).

wording_issues.issue: Several single interventions remove only part of transfer. Divergence masking leaves 0.14 of baseline (2611.02509; Qwen3-4B, raven–snail, number lists). Patching 16 relay heads lowers transfer by 46%, and relay plus identity heads by 52%, each compared with a random-head patch (2611.02509). First-divergence masking keeps +7.10 of +8.50 at 60K rows (2608.26958). In 2606.00995 the share removed depends on the intervention and the set-up. Replacing v_student removes over 50% in the main LoRA configuration, nearly all across five other LoRA configurations, and over 80% with a fine-tuned teacher. Ablating v_teacher removes nearly all. The channel also depends on the trait: single-token traits go through unembedding neighbours, while a conditional behaviour keeps 0.59 of 0.63 after neighbour masking (2606.22019).

The version lists it as a carrier. Two results go against it being necessary. Transfer survives removal of entangled-token samples (2509.23886), and a reanalysis reads Zur et al.'s deltas as animal-wide shifts (lw:kFiQ). 2609.19149 tests no transfer. On frozen Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, exact sequence scoring does not recover the positive single-token association (r = −0.050 and −0.048), and the authors say this does not identify the training-time mechanism. Causal support comes only for single-token traits in pretrained base LMs, and a conditional behaviour survives neighbour masking (2606.22019). The original does not test entanglement (its untested line).

Studies define the term differently. 2509.23886: positions where differently biased teachers would choose differently. 2609.20027 follows that definition, using counterfactual teachers fine-tuned on five animals. Divergence tokens are about 10% of its data, and its Divergence comparison restricts the loss to divergence or non-divergence tokens, each capped at 10%. 2611.02509: the 12% of tokens where two teachers' distributions separate. 2608.26958: only the first teacher–base divergence per completion, about 5.5–5.9% of tokens. Results differ across these definitions and across data types.

Fits steered teachers well, but conflicts for prompted teachers (2608.05734 r36, r38, r39 against 2606.00995 R7, R9). A single directly optimised vector matches the student in distribution but generalises worse (2610.10657). The single-direction account of the LoRA holds only below rank 64 (2606.00831).

The original's theorem covers a single small step from shared initialization. Studies test several distinct gradient claims with different outcomes. One-step alignment is weak but cumulative alignment is strong (2609.01091). Plain SGD gives 0% against Adam's 57% (2606.00995). The signal can be stored in AdamW's first moment (2608.20442). Shared hidden initialization is not necessary in a split-head toy model (2605.23645). Initial alignment is positive in a model with no transfer (2610.27943).

wording_issues.phrase: (token entanglement, divergence tokens, a steering-vector-like direction, a gradient argument)
wording_issues.issue: The list leaves out carriers that studies propose and test. These include token positions in 2606.00831: at entity tokens, early-layer FFN adapters suffice; at chat-template tokens, adapters switched on only at those positions recover the effect, with no layer restriction shown. They also include AdamW optimizer state (2608.20442), output-head compatibility (2605.23645), log-linear or teacher log-ratio structure (2602.04863, 2608.31079), a relay-head circuit (2611.02509) and per-sample log-prob shift (2606.04071).

The phrase places the mechanism in the data, but some results depend on the student or the training procedure. Head compatibility gates transfer in a toy model (2605.23645). The optimizer decides whether transfer occurs (2606.00995 R22). Removing the chat template from both training and evaluation removes transmission (2606.00831 r42).

method_sensitivity.what: Greedy decoding keeps transfer on Qwen2.5-7B (2509.23886). Under temperature 1, masking divergence tokens still usually suppresses transfer, with 'rare exceptions (e.g., penguin)'; the text names no model for the exception (2509.23886). Threshold sampling (t = 0.05) during teacher dataset generation lowers subliminal-learning success from 60% to about 28%; that section of the post names no model (lw:m5Xz). The owls README gives the same figures as 'owl' probability: 60% at temperature 1.0 and 28% with threshold p>0.05, against a 12% no-fine-tuning baseline. It is a teacher-data sampling condition, not a prompting one, and no model or fine-tuning set-up is stated for these numbers (the README's general line says Llama-3.2 1B Instruct is used for all experiments). The README and lw:m5Xz have the same authors, so this is probably one result reported twice.

On Qwen2.5-7B, loss-matched plain SGD gives a 0% cat hit rate against 57% with Adam (2606.00995). In AdamW, transplanting weights plus first moment reproduces the descendant: SSE/ZERO 0.005–0.006 for Qwen owl, over the 3-seed discovery and 4-seed replication cohorts together. A first-moment-only transplant is invisible at the cut, then grows. The text says a second-moment-only transplant stays at the no-transplant baseline (Fig. 3a caption, Qwen; about equal to ZERO for Llama, Appendix M.6) (2608.20442).

method_sensitivity.factor: How the teacher was biased (system prompt, steering vector, fine-tuning)
method_sensitivity.what: Steered teachers yield students aligned with the steering vector, and prompted teachers do not (2608.05734); vector recovery fails for prompted teachers according to the text of 2604.25783. In the poisoning setting, steering-generated data transfers less than a prompted attack (2602.04899, lw:PWpm).

method_sensitivity.factor: Adapter placement and context: LoRA rank, layer, token position, chat template, evaluation system prompt
method_sensitivity.what: The top-1 singular vector suffices only below LoRA rank 64. Entity-only or chat-template-only adapters recover the effect, and removing the chat template removes it (2606.00831). Single early-layer LoRAs suffice where late ones do not (2509.23886). Under an empty system prompt at layer 24, the three lineages' students read 0.29, 0.26 and 0.27 of their teachers (the teacher's context is not stated). Measured against the students' own matched-context projections, the appendix gives a mean of 0.301 (raw +30.73, +26.21, +28.50). Screened trait expression is 0/60 in each lineage (2609.25721).

method_sensitivity.factor: Gradient measure: one-step vs cumulative vs checkpoint-local
method_sensitivity.what: One-step gap–update correlations are +0.047 to +0.274, against +0.769 to +0.845 for 200-step drift (2609.01091). Checkpoint-local first-order predictions agree in sign in 59 of 60 intervals, while the frozen start-policy gradient fails after about step 16 (2610.41301).

With exact full-sequence scoring or within-width standardization, the single-token association turns to −0.050, −0.048, −0.049 and −0.032 on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B. On Llama-3.1, geometry correlation and specificity fall from 8B (0.1877, 0.1550) to 70B (0.1076, 0.0458) (2609.19149).

Divergence masking cuts Δgap from +2.00 to +1.10 at 10K rows but only from +8.50 to +7.10 at 60K (2608.26958). Under hard-label recovery, the optimal stopping point k* grows with the number of independent carrier sequences: 100, 190, 330, 560, 880 as M doubles from 500 (Qwen, cat, 1,000-step horizon). The text (abstract, Section 6.1, Figure 4b) says resampling from 500 prompts matches new prompts at a matched budget (2610.04907).

On Qwen2.5-7B, transfer is 90.8% from numbers, 63.1% from gibberish and 34.3% from medical answers. In the MNIST toy, real and shuffled inputs give 49.9% and 43.7% and a constant input 9.8% (2609.23260). Code carriers do not transfer on Qwen2.5-7B (2609.01091). In reasoning-response data, divergence masking leaves a significant gap (2610.18517).
